context:
Start by running w0 and updating the TODO or PR body with the current evidence
summary. Then fix only the stale command/test ratchets. Prefer extending
existing tests under `tests/unit/test_standardized_test_commands.py` and
`tests/unit/test_release_infrastructure.py` so future drift fails in the fast
lane. Treat coverage threshold changes as a policy decision, not a mechanical
edit.
description:
The release-path adversarial review found several test-command and ratchet
mismatches that create false confidence before any stronger release gate can
be made trustworthy.

Baseline evidence from 2026-05-25:
  - Required PR test jobs use fast-only pytest selection.
  - `pr-preflight-fast-tests` uses `-m fast -q`, while CI excludes
    slow/stress/resource/live tests and enforces coverage.
  - `tests/unit/test_release_infrastructure.py` is `medium`, outside the
    required fast gate, and the review run found stale workflow/template
    assertions in that file.
  - `make test-ci` is not part of mandatory CI and uses a legacy marker
    expression plus the separate `pytest-ci.ini` coverage scope.
  - CI enforces coverage at 70%, while `tests/conftest.py` only warns below
    80% when pytest-cov is active.

This TODO is the prerequisite cleanup item. It does NOT decide the final
release quality contract; it makes the existing command surfaces honest,
revalidates the stale-release-ratchet failures, and removes mismatches that
would otherwise hide or confuse release-gate work.

anti_patterns.dont: broaden `make pr-preflight` into a full release suite
anti_patterns.instead: create release-specific gates in dependent TODOs instead.

anti_patterns.dont: edit generated workflow mirrors or indexes directly
anti_patterns.instead: run the project TODO index command after edits.

anti_patterns.dont: hide currently failing release ratchets by deleting assertions
anti_patterns.instead: update them to assert the current architecture.
anti_patterns.why: those tests are the evidence trail for release confidence

deferrals.reason: Owned by `release-required-main-pr-test-contract`; this cleanup item only removes misleading command drift.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] superseded: release-required-main-pr-test-contract (the item said to own this) is already DONE, so defining the release-critical suite was resolved there.

preserves.behavior: No raw test logs or coverage files are committed; compact evidence belongs in TODO notes, PR body, or CI artifacts.
Required GitHub PR checks continue to report the existing `lint`, `test (ubuntu-latest, 3.12)`, and `ci-required-result` names unless a downstream ruleset TODO updates the required contexts.
`make pr-preflight` remains a lightweight local gate and still skips code tests for safe content-only PRs through the existing path classifier.

prior_art.concept: .github/workflows/pr.yml:code-test — reuse as authoritative required develop PR test expression
Makefile:ci-test and pr-preflight-fast-tests — extend existing local/CI command mirrors instead of adding another shell wrapper
tests/unit/test_release_infrastructure.py — repair existing release ratchets rather than adding parallel workflow tests

verifications.command: uv run --project _project/scripts -- python _project/scripts/todo_cli.py check-graph && uv run --project _project/scripts -- python _project/scripts/validate_todo.py _project/TODO/main/planning/release-test-command-ratchet-alignment.yaml
verifications.description: TODO graph remains valid after this item is moved or updated

work_units.notes:
Capture raw output under `/tmp/release-test-command-ratchet-w0/` and
commit only a compact summary in the PR body or TODO notes.

Required commands:
  - `git status --short --branch`
  - `uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/test_release_infrastructure.py -q`
  - `BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK=1 uv run -- python -m pytest --collect-only -q -n 0 -m fast tests/test_tpcds_direct.py`
  - `BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK=1 uv run -- python -m pytest --collect-only -q -n 0 -m "fast and not (slow or stress or resource_heavy or live_integration)" tests/test_tpcds_direct.py`
  - `BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK=1 uv run -- python -m pytest -c pytest-ci.ini --collect-only -q -n 0 -m "not (slow or flaky or local_only)"`

Decision gate:
  - If `test_release_infrastructure.py` no longer fails, update the work
    notes to name the fixing commit before changing tests.
  - If `make test-ci` becomes an actual required workflow target before
    implementation starts, stop and split that work into the release gate
    TODO instead of treating it as cleanup.

Implementation evidence, 2026-05-25 on branch
`todo/release-test-command-ratchet`:
  - `test_release_infrastructure.py` still failed before edits with 3
    stale assertions: PR template sections, `test.yml` matrix shape, and
    removed `release.yml:check-ci-passed`.
  - `tests/test_tpcds_direct.py -m fast` collected 3 tests; the CI marker
    expression collected 2 tests, proving local `-m fast` did not mirror
    the required CI selector.
  - `make test-ci` collection succeeded and collected 24450/24883 tests,
    so the target was stale/unwired but not dead.
work_units.summary: Re-validate the release-test command drift evidence against the current branch

work_units.notes:
Update `tests/unit/test_release_infrastructure.py` so it asserts the
current release architecture rather than the retired one:
  - `release.yml` has `dependency-bounds`, `build`, `publish`,
    `github-release`, and `test-installation`; it must not expect the
    removed `check-ci-passed` job.
  - `test.yml` must be inspected as the current job set; do not assume a
    matrix under `jobs.test` unless the workflow actually has one.
  - PR template checks must match `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`.
  - Add a narrow assertion documenting that `release.yml` itself runs no
    pytest, so future reviewers see the release-path dependency clearly.

Decision gate:
  - If the repaired assertions run in <10s and do not build artifacts,
    mark this file `fast` and `unit` so release-infrastructure drift is
    covered by mandatory fast gates.
  - If any assertion needs build/package work, split that single assertion
    into a separate `medium` test and keep the pure workflow parsing tests
    fast.
work_units.summary: Repair stale release-infrastructure ratchet tests and place them in the correct lane

work_units.notes:
Compare `Makefile:pr-preflight-fast-tests` with both required fast-test
surfaces:
  - `.github/workflows/pr.yml:code-test` for develop PRs.
  - `.github/workflows/test.yml:test` for main/release PRs.

Preferred outcome:
  - Change local preflight to use the same marker expression as CI:
    `fast and not (slow or stress or resource_heavy or live_integration)`.
  - Add a workflow/Makefile ratchet test that fails if the Makefile,
    develop PR workflow, and main PR workflow expressions drift again.

Decision gate:
  - Do not add the full coverage run to local preflight unless the runtime
    cost is explicitly accepted in the PR body. If coverage remains CI-only,
    update `Makefile` help/comments so preflight no longer claims to fully
    mirror CI.
work_units.summary: Align local preflight test selection with the required CI test job or rename the local guarantee

work_units.notes:
Decide whether `make test-ci` should survive as a broad local command.

Acceptable paths:
  - Maintain it: register any intentionally used markers in both pytest
    configs, align the coverage source with the authoritative CI scope,
    add a fast unit ratchet for the command string, and document what it
    covers that `ci-test` does not.
  - De-emphasize it: rename or update help/comments so it is not presented
    as a current CI mirror, and prefer `ci-test`/release-specific targets.

Decision gate:
  - Do not silently keep `test-ci` with divergent coverage semantics. The
    PR must state whether it is maintained, deprecated, or re-scoped.
work_units.summary: Make `test-ci` either a maintained command or remove its broad-CI implication

work_units.notes:
Pick one explicit policy:
  - Raise CI `--cov-fail-under` to 80 if the project intends 80 as the
    real floor.
  - Lower/remove the local 80 warning if 70 is the intended enforced
    release floor.
  - Keep both only if docs/comments explain 70 as blocking and 80 as
    advisory, with a test proving the warning remains non-failing.

Decision gate:
  - Do not change the threshold opportunistically to make current CI pass.
    Record the current measured coverage from the updated CI command and
    justify the selected threshold.
work_units.summary: Resolve the 70% enforced coverage floor vs 80% local warning mismatch
